verses.english: Linked Discourses 2.10
Chapter One
The Sun
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena sūriyo devaputto rāhunā asurindena gahito hoti.
verses.english: Now at that time the Sun God had been seized by Rāhu, lord of titans.

verses.pali: Atha kho sūriyo devaputto bhagavantaṁ anussaramāno tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
verses.english: Then the Sun God, recollecting the Buddha, at that time spoke this verse:
“Homage to you, Buddha, hero!
You’re free in every way.
I’ve wandered into confinement:
be my refuge!”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sūriyaṁ devaputtaṁ ārabbha rāhuṁ asurindaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha addressed Rāhu in verse concerning the Sun God:
“The Sun God has gone for refuge
to the Realized One, the perfected one.
The Buddhas have compassion for the world—
so Rāhu, release the Sun!
He is a beacon in the darkness,
the blazing sun, circle of awesome might.
Rāhu, do not swallow him as he traverses the sky.
Rāhu, release my offspring, the Sun!”

verses.pali: Atha kho rāhu asurindo sūriyaṁ devaputtaṁ muñcitvā taramānarūpo yena vepacitti asurindo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā saṁviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
verses.english: Then Rāhu, having released the Sun, rushed to see Vepacitti, lord of titans and stood to one side, shocked and awestruck.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho rāhuṁ asurindaṁ vepacitti asurindo gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Vepacitti addressed him in verse:
“Why the rush?
Rāhu, you released the Sun
and came here looking like you’re in shock:
why do you stand there so scared?”
“My head would have exploded in seven pieces,
I would have found no joy in life,
if, when enchanted by the Buddha’s verse,
I had not released the Sun.”
